summary.headline: Radico Q2 FY27 revenue Rs 1,746 crore and EBITDA margin 20.4%, with P&A volume up 36% and FY27 P&A volume guidance raised to 30%.
summary.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as the strongest quarter in company history, with IMFL volume above 10 million cases (+7% YoY), revenue of Rs 1,746 crore and EBITDA of Rs 356 crore at a 20.4% margin (+462 bps YoY). Prestige & Above (P&A) volume hit a record 5.28 million cases, up 36%, while the Regular category declined about 15% after the Andhra Pradesh route-to-market change and Maharashtra and Karnataka policy changes. Gross margin was 48.0%, up 440 bps YoY but down 109 bps QoQ, with packaging inflation costing about Rs 27 crore. The company upgraded FY27 P&A volume growth guidance to 30% and kept EBITDA margin guidance at around 20%. Leadership changes: Dilip Banthiya joined the Board as Executive Director and CFO, and Saket Somani was elevated to Deputy CFO.

segments.name: Prestige & Above (P&A)
segments.commentary: Record 5.28 million cases, up 36% YoY. Vodka grew about 49% and non-vodka P&A about 20%, against an industry P&A growth of about 5.8-6%.

segments.name: Regular
segments.commentary: Volume declined about 15% YoY, driven by the high Q2 FY26 base after the Andhra Pradesh route change and Maharashtra and Karnataka policy changes. H1 Regular volume was down 1.5%.

segments.name: IMFL vs non-IMFL margins
segments.commentary: IMFL EBITDA margin is about 24%+ in Q2; non-IMFL margin is about 9.5-10%.

segments.name: Luxury portfolio
segments.commentary: FY26 turnover was Rs 475 crore; management says it is well on track for 25% value growth in FY27. Virasat Indian Single Malt is priced at about Rs 3,500-4,000 a bottle.

segments.name: Vodka
segments.commentary: Vodka reached 6.3% of IMFL in Q2, up from 3.7% in 2025 and 4.5% in 2026. Flavoured vodka is about 75% of Radico's vodka; vodka is about 30% of Radico's volume.

segments.name: Exports / International
segments.commentary: Shipments to West Asia have recovered after the initial disruption in Feb-Mar 2026; freight costs are the main issue. Radico is now listed in 4 UK airports and in about 70 duty-free locations, with a target of 100.

guidance_outlook: FY27 P&A volume growth guidance upgraded to 30% (from prior guidance, which was revised twice this year).
EBITDA margin guidance of around 20% maintained for FY27.
Luxury portfolio value growth guidance of 25% for FY27 reiterated.
Regular category expected to grow about 1-2% from H2 onward; Maharashtra base effect expected to be largely neutralised in H2.
Management did not give FY28-29 volume numbers, but said momentum will continue and margins will keep expanding; FY28 guidance may come at year end.
Working capital build is temporary and expected to normalise in H2 FY27.
Pricing: normal P&A-to-Regular mix gap of 5-6%, and an annual price increase of 100-125 bps expected.
capex_capacity: Capex is directed to maintenance, operational efficiencies and essential capacity optimisation; no new capacity commissioning details were given in the call.
Management said it built higher inventory to offset rising grain prices, which supported Q2.
Working capital was deliberately increased to support premium growth, new launches and secure raw material and packaging, and is expected to normalise in H2.
Value engineering and packaging light-weighting are ongoing; no quantified savings were given.
demand_pricing: Vodka structural shift: vodka share of IMFL rose to 6.3% in Q2 FY27. Management expects vodka to outpace other categories over the next 3-5 years.
Karnataka: Radico grew premium volume more than 100% after duty cuts and free pricing, but Karnataka is only about 6% of salience.
Maharashtra: P&A returned to growth in Q2 as vodka reached about 10% of the state's industry.
Tamil Nadu: orders resumed on a tertiary basis from September, and Radico volumes there rose about 20%. Morpheus is the largest premium brandy in the state.
Telangana price revision: represented to the government; timing depends on the government.
UK FTA: BIO prices are expected to fall 8-10%. Management said Radico's single malts are priced above BIO and its other brands sit well below BIO cost.

Industry input-cost pass-through: industry is applying for excise price increases from November, with most state policies revised around February. Price increases in 7-8 states were already in place this quarter.
Packaging inflation: glass bottles, PET resin and laminates are affected by the West Asia conflict.
Grain (FCI ethanol allocation of 72 lakh MT) expected to stabilise prices from the November new crop season.

qa_highlights.question: What is the DRI investigation's impact on Radico, and what is the pricing freedom and lag versus input costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Banthiya said Radico is compliant and continues to import Scotch under HSN 2208, with no code change. The company sees no impact and the 20% margin guidance is unchanged. Input cost pressure of Rs 27 crore is being mitigated, and prices are expected to stabilise from November.

qa_highlights.question: Why was guidance upgraded twice when the macro environment is more challenging? Is it vodka, Karnataka, or market share gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhishek Khaitan cited the structural vodka shift (6.3% share), Karnataka growth (over 100% premium volume growth), and broad growth across states. He said momentum is as strong as in H1, with festive demand.

qa_highlights.question: What is the non-vodka P&A growth and is Maharashtra dragging it down?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said non-vodka P&A grew about 20% against an industry P&A growth of 5.8-6%, and Maharashtra P&A returned to growth. Saket Somani said Karnataka is only 6% of salience, so other states are contributing more.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjeev Banga said exports have rebounded after the initial West Asia disruption; the issue now is freight costs, which are partly absorbed by customers, with no growth slowdown in export markets.

qa_highlights.question: What is the realisation split between price and mix, and how much packaging impact was in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Banthiya said P&A realisation rose 2.2% QoQ and about 12% YoY, with price contributing 85 bps. Packaging impact was about Rs 27 crore versus Rs 30 crore in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What are the margin levers for FY28-29, and the outlook for Regular volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Saket Somani said margins will continue to expand, with vodka and luxury as higher-margin drivers, but no number was given. Banthiya expects Regular volume growth of 1-2% from H2.

qa_highlights.question: Would the spirits or luxury portfolio be affected by the UP elections?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhishek Khaitan said UP's liquor revenue of about Rs 60,000-65,000 crore is large and well-managed, and that business does not slow during elections.

risks_watch: DRI scrutiny of Scotch imports: the duty reduction from 150% to 75% may not apply to bulk Scotch imports, per press reports. The Ministry of Commerce and DRI are still studying the issue.
Packaging and grain cost volatility (glass, PET, laminates, grain) from the West Asia conflict; the margin depends on Rs 27 crore per quarter of input pressure.
Telangana price revision is pending; timing is uncertain.
Competitive intensity in vodka and in the UK, as the FTA cuts BIO prices by 8-10%.
Litigation over Spirit of Kashmyr brand is sub judice; management declined to comment.
Working capital build to be unwound in H2 FY27.
Freight costs for exports remain elevated.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on volume and premiumisation, with specific numbers provided. Cautious and non-committal on margins beyond FY27, FY28-29 volume and the DRI matter, which were deferred to later disclosure.
key_quotes: The second quarter of FY27 has been the strongest in our history with record volume , revenue and profitability.
Looking ahead, we have upgraded our Prestige & Above volume growth to 30% in FY27, and we remain confident of sustaining an EBITDA margin of around 20% for the year.
This is temporary build, and we expect it to normalize during the second half of this year.
I think guidance is something where you are sure of.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 27 crore (about 155-160 bps of gross margin; about 1.6% of net sales)

growth.why: FY27 P&A volume growth guidance raised to 30% and EBITDA margin held at around 20%, backed by demand/share gains in P&A (5.28 mn cases, +36% YoY) and mix, but no new capacity or order book was cited; Regular volume is down about 15% and the brief gives no capacity additions.

mgmt.note: Dilip Banthiya joined the Board as Executive Director and CFO, and Saket Somani was elevated to Deputy CFO; no growth plan attached to the change in the brief.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin 20.4% (+462 bps YoY) and guidance held at around 20% for FY27, with packaging cost of Rs 27 crore/quarter and grain pressure offsetting mix gains; management said margins will keep expanding beyond FY27 but gave no number.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Capex is directed to maintenance, efficiency and capacity optimisation (Rs 150-170 crore FY27 maintenance), with no new capacity commissioning details given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 P&A volume growth guidance raised to 30% after Q2 P&A volume of 5.28 mn cases (+36% YoY), and Regular volume expected to grow 1-2% from H2 after a Q2 decline of about 15%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is framed as maintenance and optimisation only, with no new plant or board approval mentioned, so a major new capex announcement is not signalled in the window.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: P&A volume guidance was raised to 30% and momentum described as as strong as H1 with festive demand, though margin guidance was only held at around 20%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Packaging (Rs 27 crore/quarter) and grain cost pressures persist, and the Telangana price revision and DRI Scotch import issue are unresolved, though management says the DRI has no impact and the 20% margin is unchanged.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Working capital was built partly to support new launches, but no specific product or launch date was named; vodka (6.3% of IMFL) and luxury (FY26 Rs 475 crore, targeting 25% growth) are the growth levers.

rows.label: Annual price increase of 100-125 bps and Telangana revision
rows.why: Management expects an annual price increase of 100-125 bps, with industry excise price increases sought from November and 7-8 states already raising prices, though the Telangana revision timing depends on government.

rows.label: Duty-free and UK airport distribution to 100 locations
rows.why: Radico is in 4 UK airports and about 70 duty-free locations against a target of 100, with West Asia exports already recovered and freight costs the main issue.

rows.label: Working capital unwind in H2 FY27
rows.why: Working capital was deliberately built to secure inventory against grain and packaging inflation and is expected to normalise in H2 FY27, which would support cash flow.

tone.note: Management was confident on P&A volume (+36%), vodka share (6.3%) and Karnataka, but cautious on margins beyond FY27, FY28-29 volume and the DRI Scotch import matter; analysts pressed on guidance upgrades in a tougher macro and on input-cost pass-through.
